title: The Last Orchard on Six
summary: On Habitat Six, a failing hatch gives grafting apprentice Nia Sol one afternoon to save the old pear tree where her mother marked her height. The answer is written in six scars beneath its bark.
coverAlt: The Last Orchard on Six. Nia, a young Black grafter in turquoise coveralls and a mustard headband, cradles a tiny pear cutting beside a pale, twisting fruit tree. Through the orbital greenhouse windows a blue planet curves away.
style: European ligne claire in turquoise, ochre and bone, with cinematic three-tier pages.

pages.alt: Habitat Six curves above a striped blue planet. In its glass orchard, Nia holds a yellow pear below a fruiting branch. Ivo smiles over the rail. An amber warning lamp brings Nia, Ivo and two neighbors up short.
pages.transcript:
Nia: See that gold one, Ivo? Sunday. That’s when it’ll give.
Ivo: You say that every Sunday.
Nia: And one Sunday I’ll be right.

pages.alt: A cream-uniformed engineer lifts a floor grille under the pear tree. She points at a gauge and the cracked coupling on a turquoise pipe. Nia stands between the pale trunk and a descending amber gate.
pages.transcript:
Engineer: Look under the roots. The return pipe has pushed the hatch track crooked.
Engineer: We seal this bay at eighteen hundred. If the hatch won’t shut, six homes lose their cooling.
Nia: Then we move the tree.

pages.alt: Nia puts one red-gloved hand against a neat row of height marks and a thumbprint on the gray bark. Beside a cargo cart, Ivo opens a rolled canvas sling. Two workers fit the sling around the tree from opposite sides.
pages.transcript:
Nia: Mum stood me here every birthday. I finally passed her thumbprint.
Ivo: Put your hands on the cart, then. Let’s find out what can move.
Nia: Easy. She doesn’t like being rushed.

pages.alt: Nia pulls the winch rope while the engineer watches the root ball lift. Beneath the tree, thick roots twist around a brass joint in a turquoise pipe. Nia lowers the sling while Ivo reaches under a heavy connector.
pages.transcript:
Ivo: Up two fingers. Hold it there.
Nia: Stop! The pipe is coming with it.
Nia: Down. I know. Down.

pages.alt: Ivo shows Nia a diagonal join in the pear tree. Her glove traces a row of six healed grafts with different brass tags. They open a sepia picture of six travelers holding branches at a rocket launch.
pages.transcript:
Ivo: You keep calling her one tree. Run your hand along the first fork.
Nia: A graft scar. There’s another. And another.
Ivo: Six families brought one twig each. There wasn’t room on the launch for an orchard. So they made one.

pages.alt: Nia looks across the station at a curve of lit windows filled with tiny trees and household objects. At a workbench she sorts tags onto colored cloths. Ivo places his pruning shears in her gloved hand.
pages.transcript:
Nia: Every flat on the ring has a little pear stock. Mum used ours to dry her socks.
Nia: We can take all six varieties. They don’t have to share a trunk this time.
Ivo: You have an hour. Take the good shears.

pages.alt: Tala blocks a round laundry doorway with her arms folded. Nia opens both hands beside a small rootstock and a line of clean linen. Tala holds her door open and points down a long curve of neighboring doors.
pages.transcript:
Tala: When that tree had fruit, we got the bruised ones. Now you want my window?
Nia: Your window. Your pears. You’ll pick the first one yourself.
Tala: Then no master key. Knock at every door.

pages.alt: At the orchard bench Nia and Ivo look over a row of differently colored bundles and cut branches. Their hands hold a green shoot against a rootstock and wind tape around the join. Tala touches the finished graft as a boy watches from behind the laundry steam.
pages.transcript:
Nia: Two buds from each branch. One at its new home. One next door, in case.
Ivo: My hands shake at the last wrap. You finish it.
Nia: Here. Feel how the two pieces hold each other.

pages.alt: In a yellow kitchen an older man moves a blue-and-white teapot while Nia holds a new plant. A mechanic in an ochre scarf takes another graft among purple tools. Along a bank of station doors Nia examines the colored cloths and one empty hook.
pages.transcript:
Window Two: Move the kettle. This one likes the morning light.
Window Four: The pink-fleshed one? My dad used to put salt on those.
Nia: Five colors on the rail. Where’s the little silver tag?

pages.alt: A little silver fish tag hangs from a high pear branch. Beside the ladder, Ivo shows Nia a matching fish pendant on a cord. He steadies the ladder while she climbs into the pale branches.
pages.transcript:
Ivo: In the crown. I left that branch for last.
Ivo: My sister carried it through launch. She slept with the bundle down her shirt.
Nia: You hold the ladder. I’ll bring your sister’s branch down.

pages.alt: At the control console the engineer looks up as Nia stretches across two branches. A yellow pear slips toward Nia's open palm while her other hand guards two cuttings. Below her, the neighbors catch the pear in a canvas sling.
pages.transcript:
Engineer: Two minutes to the seal. Make them count.
Nia: Oh. Sunday.
Nia: I can’t catch both.

pages.alt: Ivo leans over Nia's shoulder as she offers a leafy cutting to the boy in the blue window. Beside his paper rocket, he helps fasten the new graft to a little trunk. The lit doors stand open along the curved corridor as the big greenhouse hatch closes.
pages.transcript:
Window Six: They said the orchard was going away.
Nia: It’s coming in. Will you make room?
Ivo: Eighteen hundred. Six doors.

pages.alt: In a child's room, a brown graft bends in a terracotta pot. The boy shines his reading lamp on it while Nia sits beside him. He walks with her to the next flat and knocks on its yellow door.
pages.transcript:
Five Weeks Later: Five windows showed green. At the sixth, the bud was the color of an old tea leaf.
Boy: I did everything. I even took the lamp off my rocket.
Nia: I believe you. Come knock with me.

pages.alt: Tala draws back hanging linen to reveal two tags on her small tree. An unfurled green leaf sits beside the silver fish tag. Tala, Nia and the boy laugh as they carry the whole pot through a turquoise door.
pages.transcript:
Tala: You two looking for silver?
Boy: That new leaf was ours all this time?
Tala: Ours on this side of the door. Yours on that side. Hold the pot level.

pages.alt: A taller boy lifts a ripe pear beside a silver tree tag. Nia, Ivo and the neighbors sit around little plates of fruit on a pale bench. Through the windows of the orbital ring, the group can be seen sharing slices above the blue planet.
pages.transcript:
Three Years Later: It took three summers under the lamps before the first pear came free in a child’s hand.
Ivo: Is that my sister’s pear?
Boy: It’s Sunday. There’s enough for a slice each.
